comment: Registry of all pretrained model variants. Each module has a 'current' symlink (current.pt) that configs should reference for stable resolution. Variants are immutable; never overwrite an existing variant file.

phone_extractor.selection_note: Select phone extractors by the phonetic-contrast probe (analysis/probe_phone_extractor.py: effective_rank/temporal_contrast), NOT by cosine-similarity to HuBERT. Cos-sim rewards consistency with a (possibly smeared) target, not phonetic separability -- it misled us twice (lesson 2.2). The upstream jp_122 has the richest representation of all variants (even on English clips) and is the empirical 'worked great' baseline; our English-distillation variants (v1/v2) were regressions.

variants.note: Upstream Beatrice original (122_checkpoint_03000000.pt). Richest/sharpest phonetic representation of all variants, even on English clips. Empirical 'worked great' baseline. Restored to current 2026-06-02.
v1 English distillation; under-trained reproduction, less rich than upstream jp_122

REGRESSION: noise-robust+target-mix recipe collapsed phonetic contrast (-34% effective rank vs en_clean_580k) -> 'big tongue' mumbled conversions. High target cos-sim (0.84) was the lesson-2.2 trap. Do NOT use.

pitch_estimator.selection_note: Probe (analysis/probe_pitch_estimator.py, vs pyworld GT) shows all three are close (<0.8 st err, corr 0.89-0.95). jp_104 upstream is the most noise-robust (best on noisy input) and competitive on clean; the noise-robust vctk_nr showed NO advantage (worst on noisy). Reverted to upstream jp_104 to match the full 'worked great' upstream stack with jp_122. Pitch is not where quality problems live.

variants.note: Upstream Beatrice original. Most noise-robust in probe; restored to current 2026-06-02.
